label: PF Backlog 568
title: Delivery lane runs in long-lived API process: loaded code goes stale after develop merges (3 blocked/failed lanes 2026-10-10; restarts manual)
body: Root cause: python -m api.app imports modules once at process start; every PR merged to develop leaves the RUNNING server (and its in-process delivery/worker/jobs code) on the startup snapshot. Symptoms this session: heartbeat writes missing, stuck-reaping absent, worktree-prune on release missing, FEATURE_PR lane failing gates fixed hours earlier (dash app_boot SyntaxError + 'no quality-gate record'). RCCA: no freshness contract between tree state and executing process - fail-open on stale code.

objective: Lane/worker execution always uses current develop code: run delivery jobs as short-lived subprocesses against the fast-forwarded tree (kills the bug class); fail-closed freshness guard (loaded sha != develop sha -> refuse + prompt restart); surface code sha in status/health.
acceptance_criteria: delivery/worker job entry executes on tree code (subprocess CLI) or refuses when server snapshot is stale
loaded code_sha vs develop sha mismatch surfaced in status/health output
regression test simulating a stale process detects the mismatch
out_of_scope: hot-reloading of the web server itself (subprocess job execution is enough)
approach: subprocess-first: expose deliver/drain via a fresh python -m core.delivery CLI per lane trigger; stamp code_sha at api startup; health/status compares vs develop sha; remaining in-process paths guarded by the sha check (belt+braces).
verification: Objective achieved: Delivery lane runs in long-lived API process: loaded code goes stale after develop merges (3 blocked/failed lanes 2026-10-10; restarts manual)
risks: subprocess job needs structured result handoff back to the job record
sha comparison must tolerate dirty local trees (compare commit, not content)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/code_analyzer.py, core/code_executor.py, core/code_quality_gate.py, core/control_plane.py
